title: [Bug]: failed to connect **:53100
body: I am upgrading a standalone Milvus deployment from 2.2.12 to 2.3.0. I stopped Docker Compose, updated docker-compose.yml, pulled the new images, replaced milvus.yml with the official version, and started the deployment again, but Milvus fails to connect on port 53100. I attached the Milvus log and copies of my Milvus and Docker Compose configuration files.

symptoms_visible: After upgrading my standalone deployment from Milvus 2.2.12 to 2.3.0, Milvus does not start successfully and reports a failed connection on port 53100.
N0.label: N0 standalone upgrade fails

symptoms_visible: I tried the newer 2.3.x Docker image, but the standalone container still does not start; QueryNode reports 'UnexpectedError: Error:DirExist:Operation not permitted' and then panics.
N1_x.label: N1_x newer image exposes operation-not-permitted failure

symptoms_visible: The standalone container still panics with 'Operation not permitted' while starting QueryNode.
N2.label: N2 host ownership and launch user checked

symptoms_visible: After changing the Milvus volume target to /var/lib/milvus/data and checking the host directory, the container still does not start and the error remains.
N3_x.label: N3_x volume-path change aftermath

symptoms_visible: After adding seccomp:unconfined to the standalone service, the issue is solved and Milvus starts successfully.
N_terminal.label: N_terminal startup restored with seccomp override

symptoms_visible: After adding seccomp:unconfined to the standalone service, the issue is solved and Milvus starts successfully.
N_terminal_early.label: N_terminal_early direct seccomp resolution

solution.intent: Use a newer 2.3.x Docker image containing the merged startup fix and retry the upgrade.
solution.concrete_example: Pull a newer Milvus 2.3.x image containing the merged fix, recreate the standalone container, and check whether it starts.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c16-c23: maintainers said the earlier startup flaw was merged and available in a newer image, but the reporter's later 2.3.x upgrade attempt still failed. The new log showed a QueryNode 'DirExist:Operation not permitted' panic, so updating alone did not resolve the reported inability to upgrade.

question_patterns: What are the owner and permissions of the host directories mounted into the Milvus container?
Can you run pwd and ls -l on the Milvus, etcd, and MinIO volume directories?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The volumes are under /home/data/volumes. The etcd, milvus, and minio directories are owned by root:root and show drwxr-xr-x permissions.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The Milvus directory is owned by another user and has no write or execute permission for the account running Docker.
The same directories are root-owned but use mode 755 with slightly different timestamps.

question_patterns: Which user are you using to launch Docker Compose?
Are you starting Docker as root or as another account?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: Yes, I am currently the root user when I launch it.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am launching Docker as an unprivileged account that cannot access the root-owned host directory.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c32-c36: maintainers asked for the host-directory permissions and launch user. The reporter pasted the raw directory listing and confirmed Docker was being launched as root; this evidence weakens a simple host ownership mismatch but does not itself identify seccomp.

solution.intent: Treat the error as a volume-path or filesystem-permission problem by mounting the host Milvus directory at /var/lib/milvus/data and checking access.
solution.concrete_example: Change the volume mapping to /home/data/volumes/milvus:/var/lib/milvus/data, verify the host directory permissions, and restart the standalone container.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c24-c33: maintainers initially interpreted the QueryNode message as a local cache directory permission problem and asked the reporter to change the volume target. The reporter made the persistent Compose change and returned a failure mark and new log; startup remained broken.

solution.intent: Allow the Milvus standalone container to issue the system calls blocked by Docker's seccomp profile by adding security_opt with seccomp:unconfined, then restart and verify startup.
solution.concrete_example:
Under the standalone service in docker-compose.yml, add:
security_opt:
  - seccomp:unconfined
Then recreate the container and confirm that Milvus starts without the QueryNode 'Operation not permitted' panic.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the literal 'Operation not permitted' panic, root-owned directory listing, root launch user, and failed volume-path attempt. Concluding that Docker's seccomp policy rather than ordinary directory ownership blocked a required syscall is the technical inference made by the maintainers.

edges.comment: Reporter system, c37-c43: after similar Docker deployments were connected to the same error, LoveEachDay proposed security_opt with seccomp:unconfined and explained that seccomp limits container system calls. The reporter subsequently confirmed that the issue was solved.

solution.intent: Directly test whether Docker's seccomp profile is blocking Milvus by adding security_opt with seccomp:unconfined to the standalone service, then restart and verify startup.
solution.concrete_example: Add security_opt: [seccomp:unconfined] to the standalone service, recreate the container, and report whether Milvus starts normally.

edges.comment: Shortcut copy of the accepted fix so an agent proposing the correct Docker seccomp change immediately can match an edge. It skips the later QueryNode log, permission checks, and falsified volume-path attempt.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify Docker's seccomp restrictions as the accepted cause of the QueryNode 'Operation not permitted' startup failure, rather than treating the 53100 message itself as an independent network-port problem.

The diagnosis must be grounded in the startup error and, when collected, the evidence that Docker was launched as root with accessible root-owned host directories and that changing the volume target did not resolve startup.
Must recommend adding security_opt with seccomp:unconfined to the Milvus standalone service and recreating the container.
Must not claim that merely updating the image or changing the Milvus volume path is sufficient; both directions failed to restore startup in the reporter's deployment.
Must ask the reporter to verify that Milvus starts after the seccomp change before declaring the issue resolved.

persona_hint.experience_level: Operationally capable Docker Compose user who can upgrade images and configuration, inspect container logs, edit volume mappings, and run shell permission checks as root, but relies on maintainers for Milvus internals and Linux container-security diagnosis.
persona_hint.communication_style: Informal, persistent, and cooperative; supplies logs and command output, asks direct follow-up questions, and reports whether each requested configuration change worked.
